record.original_question: Extend the geodesic and Hamiltonian Euler-Arnold framework from Lie groups to Lie groupoids in a way that also covers elasticity theory, not only multiphase and vortex-sheet fluid models.

evidence.quote: Problem 2. Extend the geodesic and Hamiltonian descriptions of the Euler-Arnold equations on Lie groupoids to problems of elasticity theory. Many other open problems discussed below for the Euler equations related to diffeomorphism Lie groups can also be posed for the corresponding Lie groupoids, see e.g. Sections 5, 7, and 13. For instance, it is natural to extends Arnold’s study of the differential geometry of infinite-dimensional groups to those groupoids in view of possible applications to fluid stability problems.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Recall Arnold's framework: given a (possibly infinite-dimensional) Lie group $G$ with Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ and a (weak) right- or left-invariant Riemannian metric induced by an inner product on $\mathfrak{g}$, the geodesic equation on $G$ reduces to an evolution equation on $\mathfrak{g}$ called the Euler–Arnold equation. Equivalently, it is the Hamiltonian equation on the dual $\mathfrak{g}^{*}$ with respect to the Lie–Poisson structure and the Hamiltonian induced by the metric. This framework realizes the Euler equations of an ideal incompressible fluid as the geodesic flow on the group of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms and the rigid body equations as a geodesic flow on $SO(3)$.

A Lie groupoid is a small category $\mathcal{G} \rightrightarrows M$ whose objects form a manifold $M$, whose morphisms form a manifold $\mathcal{G}$, and whose source, target, identity, inverse, and composition maps are smooth, with source and target submersions. Its infinitesimal counterpart is a Lie algebroid $A \to M$ with anchor $\rho: A \to TM$ and a Lie bracket on sections of $A$, and the dual bundle $A^{*}$ carries a natural linear Poisson structure generalizing the Lie–Poisson structure on $\mathfrak{g}^{*}$. Given a fibrewise inner product on $A$, one obtains a sub-Riemannian or Riemannian structure on $\mathcal{G}$ that is invariant under groupoid multiplication, and the associated geodesic flow descends to a Hamiltonian system on $A^{*}$, which is the Euler–Arnold equation on the groupoid. Known examples in fluid dynamics include geodesic descriptions of generalized (multiphase) flows and of vortex-sheet motions as Hamiltonian systems on appropriate diffeomorphism groupoids.

Problem. Develop a geodesic and Hamiltonian Euler–Arnold formalism on a suitable Lie groupoid $\mathcal{G} \rightrightarrows M$ (with associated Lie algebroid $A \to M$, anchor $\rho$, invariant fibrewise metric, and Lie–Poisson structure on $A^{*}$) such that the resulting equations describe systems of continuum elasticity theory. More precisely:

(a) Identify a Lie groupoid (or family of groupoids) generalizing the diffeomorphism group setting, together with an invariant (possibly degenerate) fibrewise inner product on its Lie algebroid, whose induced geodesic equations on $\mathcal{G}$ recover the equations of motion of elastic continua (for instance nonlinear elastodynamics of a hyperelastic body, with stored-energy function playing the role of a kinetic-like term, or a Lagrangian/Hamiltonian system on a configuration space of embeddings).

(b) Write down the corresponding Euler–Arnold equation on $A$ (or its dual $A^{*}$) as the reduction of the geodesic flow, identify the Lie–Poisson Hamiltonian, and verify that the unreduced geodesic equation on $\mathcal{G}$ coincides with the elasticity equations of motion.

(c) Establish the analogue of Arnold's stability and curvature theory in this groupoid setting and apply it to stability questions for elastic media.

Goal: produce a framework that simultaneously encompasses the known groupoid descriptions of multiphase fluids and vortex sheets and the equations of elasticity theory.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is stated as an open research direction in a recent survey of open problems in geometric hydrodynamics. Related groupoid approaches to geometric mechanics and to generalized/multiphase fluid flows exist (e.g., Fusca's thesis and the Izosimov–Khesin paper on generalized fluid flows), but no published work appears to carry out the Euler–Arnold groupoid program for elasticity theory. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: A groupoid approach to geometric mechanics (D. Fusca, thesis)
status_evidence.snippet: Groupoid framework for geometric mechanics applied to multiphase and vortex-sheet hydrodynamics.
status_evidence.claim: Existing groupoid formalism covers multiphase fluids and vortex sheets, but not elasticity.

status_evidence.title: Geometry of generalized fluid flows
status_evidence.snippet: Generalized flows, multiphase fluids, and vortex sheets correspond to geodesics on groupoids of multiphase diffeomorphisms, Hamiltonian w.r.t. a Poisson structure on a dual Lie algebroid.
status_evidence.claim: State of the art for groupoid Euler-Arnold; elasticity not addressed.
